request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

tools.name: get_fold_detail
tools.description: Get the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown for a completed experiment run. Use this to compare fold-level consistency between runs.

output.text:
**Pick: run 3.** LightGBM with the `no_size` feature set, `class_weight` for imbalance, num_leaves 8, and 600 trees. My confidence is low, at 0.45.

| Run | Model | Features | PR-AUC mean | SD | Prec@50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LightGBM, 15 leaves | all | 0.7346 | 0.0677 | 0.764 |
| 2 | Random forest | no_size | 0.6871 | 0.0758 | 0.736 |
| 3 | LightGBM, 8 leaves | no_size | 0.7142 | 0.0705 | 0.772 |

- **Run 2 is out.** It is clearly the weakest. It trails run 1 by about 0.05 PR-AUC and is worse in every fold.
- **Runs 1 and 3 are statistically tied.** The 0.020 PR-AUC gap between them is about 0.3 of a fold SD, far below the one-SD bar (about 0.07). Run 1 did beat run 3 in all 5 folds, but only by 0.007 to 0.041. The folds are paired, so that consistency is real. It is still small next to the fold-to-fold swings, which run from about 0.62 to 0.80 and are driven by the folds, not the models.
- **Why run 3 over run 1.** Under the tie-break rule I take the more conservative model. Run 3 has fewer leaves and drops the size features. Size features can mostly track how big a provider is, or how often it gets audited, instead of suspicious behaviour. The label's origin is undocumented, so that risk matters. Run 3 also has the higher Prec@50 (0.772 vs 0.764), which is closer to what the ~100-provider queue needs.
- **Run 1 is a reasonable alternative.** It uses a plainer pipeline, with no class weighting, and has the best mean PR-AUC. A reviewer could defend it, which is why my confidence is below 0.5.
- **Possible leakage.** A ROC-AUC of about 0.94 and PR-AUC of about 0.73 against a 9.35% base rate is strong. That is true even for the `no_size` runs, so size is not the only driver. The label may come from rules applied to the claims themselves, so the model could be reproducing those rules instead of finding fraud. I would treat these scores as an upper bound until the label source is documented.
- **Time-based check still missing.** Claims span only about 13 months, and I can't tell whether the folds respect time or provider grouping. I would check that before relying on the numbers.

Further search is unlikely to help, since the candidates are within noise. The remaining uncertainty is about the labels, which more tuning won't fix. I'm setting stop=true.

**chosen_run: 3, confidence: 0.45, stop: true**
